alignments.note: Dative pronoun: the case preposition rides with the word under rule 21's determinerless clause, no article standing to anchor it.

The ASV renders `εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν` as *it is a very small thing*, writing no English preposition anywhere for the phrase; rule 36 leaves a preposition empty exactly where English realizes it nowhere at all.

Anarthrous substantival superlative expanded with a supplied determiner and generic noun; rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped to anarthrous Greek and keeps the head on the adjective, with *very* an intensifying helper on the superlative.
Conjunction realized by the complementizer that introduces its English clause (rule 40).
Subject, modal and passive auxiliary ride with the verb; head on the lexical *judged* (rules 9 and 17).
Adjective rendered by the English possessive *man's*; the ASV's gloss note (*Greek day*) confirms that *judgment* answers to the noun and not to this word.
`ἡμέρας` rendered *judgment*, as the ASV's own gloss note records.
The ASV writes a single *not* for this negative connective; no second negative word stands to carry the negation, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it. Discontinuity is licensed by rule 15.
Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun (rules 9 and 17).

Reflexive pronoun rendered by the three-word emphatic *mine own self*; head on the *-self* word under rule 17, as rule 107 heads a two-word emphatic on *self* rather than on the plain possessive standing first.
